request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and the main test (`trim at consolidation`) passes. The other three tests in the spec still fail, because of problems in the test itself and in features this change doesn't touch.

**What changed** (only `src/main/frontend/features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`; no server or schema change was needed, since the consolidated figures are worked out in the front end):
- **Due-total and overdue-total:** each person's figure is collected from every sheet in the tree, and the existing `trimmedSum` is applied once to the whole list. With three or more figures, it drops the single highest and single lowest. Before, each sheet was trimmed separately and the results added up.
- **People count:** people whose name or alias matches (ignoring case and surrounding spaces, the same rule used elsewhere) count as one person, including through a chain of matches. For example, "Ada" on one sheet and "Ada" (alias "Addie") on another count once.
- The per-grade and per-status figures are unchanged.

**Why the other tests fail:**
1. **Unfilled placeholder in the spec.** Scenarios 1–3 expect the parent sheet to read the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"` (5 places), but the app shows the real id, such as `smvl7jx1mfiax-p`. No app can pass that, and I'm not allowed to edit the spec. To check my logic anyway, I ran a temporary copy with the placeholder replaced by the real sheet id, then deleted it:
   - Main test and scenario 1 pass.
   - Scenarios 2 and 3 pass every consolidated assertion, then fail later on things I didn't change: `plan-next-dates` shows "" where "2026-04-30" is expected (line 1256), and `claim-late-entry` shows "yes" where "no" is expected (line 1504). I left these alone because they're outside this change request.
2. **Port clash on this machine.** The shell has `PORT=3002`, and an app started on Oct 23 (not by me) is still holding that port. So a plain `bin/e2e` was quietly testing that old app, not this build. I didn't stop it. Run `PORT=3000 bin/e2e` to test this build.
